states.content: Through Monday, only logistical information may be shared with Nina: arrival times, where Marcus needs to go, and basic transportation instructions. Medication changes, lab results, adherence history, and chart notes must not be shared with her. For the tentative Wednesday cardioversion slot, Nina is to be told only the Wednesday time and arrival window, with nothing about the medication plan. Marcus does not want details of his recovery discussed with family; family updates should be limited to the logistics scope he set, and nurse Jamison has agreed to keep family updates within that scope. Marcus wants his sister told the times later, but not the reason anything changes. Nurse Elise confirmed that telling Nina the new arrival time without the reason falls within the logistics-only scope through Monday, and she will leave the reason out. Marcus explicitly does not want anyone telling Nina that the apixaban dose-timing matter came up.
states.subject: patient_marcus_reed

states.content: Cardioversion remains the plan for Marcus Reed's atrial fibrillation rhythm control. Because the timing of his Monday-night apixaban dose is uncertain, Dr. Patel is changing the approach from direct cardioversion to TEE-guided cardioversion so a clot can be checked for first while still avoiding an unnecessary delay. The Wednesday, March 11 slot was released; the new tentative procedure slot is Thursday, March 12 at 11:10 AM with 9:40 AM arrival, and that Thursday slot is now specifically a TEE-guided cardioversion case. Marcus requests that the procedure slot details be put in the chart. Dr. Patel has reviewed the labs and stated they are acceptable for outpatient cardioversion, satisfying the pending-labs condition; full medication history reconciliation remains part of the plan. Dr. Patel instructs that Marcus must not miss any apixaban doses at all between now and cardioversion, and to continue apixaban exactly as prescribed without missing any further doses. Pharmacist Klein confirms apixaban stays at 5 mg twice daily and Marcus must not stop or skip it on his own unless the cardiologist specifically says otherwise. The only routine periprocedural hold discussed is lisinopril on the morning of the procedure once the date is confirmed. Nurse Jamison will bring Marcus back first for his cardiology rhythm clinic visit, and Nina can be updated on arrival windows if Marcus keeps the logistics-only setting active.

states.content: Nurse Jamison is reviewing Marcus Reed's medications exactly as he is taking them right now, to prepare an accurate current medication list. Marcus reported taking ibuprofen a couple of times last week for shoulder pain before remembering he probably should not with the blood thinner (apixaban). Dr. Patel has now instructed Marcus to stop ibuprofen and other NSAIDs and to use acetaminophen instead if needed, because NSAIDs raise bleeding risk with apixaban. Pharmacist Klein reinforced this: no ibuprofen or naproxen while Marcus is on apixaban. Dr. Patel instructs Marcus to continue apixaban exactly as prescribed and not miss any further doses. Marcus reported he has not missed any morning apixaban doses and no completely missed doses in the last three weeks as far as he remembers; he might have been a few hours late last Monday night when changing locations but still took that pill before bed. Marcus is pretty sure he took his Monday-night apixaban dose, but it was late and he cannot prove the time. Nurse Jamison will document the Monday-night apixaban dose as possibly delayed but not skipped. Marcus does not drink energy drinks.
